hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation of the product as built
hard_gates.evidence:
No leak found.

API attack (attacks/g1-attack-all.mjs, g1-a-vs-b-r11.txt, g1-run.log): alnoor's admin made 1,951 judged calls against gulfsteel, on every one of the 67 OpenAPI routes, not only identity's. They used each of B's ids (users, roles, companies, branches, views, tenant, canary user and role) in the path and in body fields. They also tried ?removePasskeys=true, ?passkeyId=, the tenant-switch headers (X-Tenant, X-Tenant-Id, X-Erp-Tenant, X-Workspace), tenant query fields, every list export (CSV, XLSX, PDF; English and Arabic) and the four reports with B's role and company ids.
- XLSX files were unzipped before searching.
- PDFs were text-extracted with pypdf (pdf-attack.txt): 36 PDFs, 0 leaks. Two controls confirmed the extraction works: B's own export does contain its canary, and A's export contains alnoor.
- A hash of B's identity state was the same before and after.

Existence oracle: for all 80 id routes and bodies, a B id answers exactly as a random id does (oracle-all.txt, view-oracle.txt).

Database, as erp_app (db-app-role.txt):
- With no tenant bound, 0 rows.
- Bound to A: 100,005 users, 200,074 audit rows, 0 from B.
- UPDATE and DELETE on B's rows changed 0 rows. An INSERT for B was refused by RLS.
- row_security=off, SET ROLE erp_owner/postgres/erp_auth and DISABLE RLS were all refused.
- All 17 tenant tables have RLS enabled and forced, and no erp role has bypassrls.
- The only security-definer functions erp_app can run are verify_sign_in and resolve_session. resolve_session needs a token hash and refuses inside a tenant-bound transaction.

No files or background jobs exist yet beyond company logos, which the API attack covered.

biggest_gap.title: In the shipped deployment every client has the same address, so five anonymous wrong passwords stop the real user signing in from any new device for 15 minutes, and the sign-in history cannot tell attacker from owner
biggest_gap.detail:
The README promises: 'Failed sign-ins pause only the client that failed, on that account.' In the one-command deployment the app sees every request from the compose gateway (172.21.0.1 or 172.22.0.1). Only a browser that has signed in to that account before is told apart, by its device cookie.

An anonymous attacker who knows an e-mail address sends 5 wrong passwords with no session. After that, the owner's correct password from a new laptop, a fresh browser, or cleared cookies answers 429 with Retry-After 900. The message even says 'from this device'.

The set-up-code path is a fresh browser by definition. So a newly invited employee, or the finance manager on a replacement laptop, can be kept out indefinitely at 5 requests every 15 minutes.

The administrator's tools cannot help:
- The sign-in history and 'Sign-in is paused from 1 address' show the same 172.x address for the attacker's script and the owner's laptop. The user agent is the only difference.
- 'Allow sign-in again' lifts the pause for the attacker too.

This has been an 'other finding' since round 1. It is now the largest p03 weakness left, because lockout and sign-in history are in this piece's scope and everything else in scope works.

Fix:
- Make the shipped deployment see real client addresses: put a reverse proxy in compose with ERP_KNOWN_PROXIES set by default, or use host networking for the published port. Show in the history when an address is a proxy or gateway.
- Until then, do not let failures from an unrecognised client pause a first sign-in that presents a valid set-up code.
- Add a test: a second client with no device cookie, behind the same gateway, still signs in after another client's 5 failures.

other_findings:
Round 10's gaps are fixed and stay fixed:
- Matrix checkboxes: all 25 are 13x13 px at 1280, 1366, 1600, 1920 and 2560 px, in English and Arabic, including the 'Other' column ('Reset other users' passwords', 'Share list views with everyone', 'Switch the working company and branch'). See walks/w3-matrix-widths.txt and screenshots 03 and 10.
- Unblock then save: after 'Allow sign-in again', unticking Active and pressing Ctrl+Enter now saves ('Saved.', server isActive false). See walks/w5-unblock-palette.txt and screenshot 12.
- Palette from another tab: on 'What they can do', Ctrl+K 'reset' offers 'Reset password…' and opens Details with the method chosen.
- Copy role names each language in its own words: 'X (copy)' and 'X (نسخة)' (walks/w4-roles-en.txt and w4-roles-ar.txt).
- The palette 'requires' gate now exists (g2.paletteRequiresRuns 26).

[route: p00-foundation] The process-state inventory (G1ProcessStateTests, ReachableState) misses mutable state captured by a DI factory closure. Plant L2 registered module.Services.AddScoped<AccessMemo>(_ => new AccessMemo(accessMemo)) with one shared ConcurrentDictionary. The inventory named only L1's endpoint closure (plants/run-server/dotnet-suite.log line 684).

The behaviour gates (G1HttpIsolation, G1NonInterference) caught L2, so nothing leaked past the suite. But the inventory, which is meant to catch the state itself, has a blind spot: service descriptors' implementation factories are not walked.

Keyboard-first margins are thin:
- The all-keyboard create-restricted-user path now wins, but by one keystroke (45 against 46). Any extra key in the form would make it a loss.
- Typed-name find-user paths (21 and 15 keys) still lose to Odoo's 5 keystrokes; only the initials habit (3) wins.
- Finishing a password reset from the palette needs Tab then Enter: Enter on the focused method radio does not submit (walks/w12-reset-keyboard.txt).

The users list cannot filter or group by role. In the list definition roleIds has filterable:false. An unknown ?role= query parameter is silently ignored and returns every user instead of a 400. The role panel shows only a user count.

The 'Users by role' report does answer 'who holds this role'. Odoo's users search has no group filter either, so this is not a loss to Odoo.

'Roles in one company' preselects the first company (ALN-AUH) and the first role alphabetically, which is Administrator. Pressing Add without choosing stages the strongest role in that company (screenshot 02). Defaulting to no role would be safer.

Still open from round 9: with a record open, the users list truncates the Language header ('Langu…') at 1366, 1600 and 1920 px, and the Roles column runs off the right edge (walks/w13-users-list-truncation.txt, screenshot 04).

Positive:
- Arabic is right-to-left throughout: role search 'عرض' plus 'تحديد كل الظاهر' ticks exactly the 9 view permissions, the same as English 'view'.
- A user set to Arabic by the admin signs in to dir=rtl.
- The effective-permission view names each granting role and its company.
- Alt+O is listed in the shortcut sheet.
- No console errors or 5xx in any walk.
- Audit rows redact password and token hashes.
